questions.question_english: Which landmark guidelines formulated by the Supreme Court of India laid down the foundational framework for the enactment of the POSH Act, 2013?
options_english: Nilabati Behera Guidelines
D.K. Basu Guidelines
Vishaka Guidelines
M.C. Mehta Guidelines
questions.explanation_english: In the landmark judgment of Vishaka and others v. State of Rajasthan (1997) 6 SCC 241; AIR 1997 SC 3011, the Supreme Court of India acknowledged the severe legislative void regarding sexual harassment of working women. Exercising its powers under Article 32 and invoking Articles 14, 15, 19(1)(g), and 21 of the Constitution along with international human rights obligations under CEDAW (Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), the Supreme Court laid down binding directions known as the 'Vishaka Guidelines'. These guidelines served as the law of the land under Article 141 of the Constitution until the POSH Act was formally enacted in 2013. In contrast, D.K. Basu guidelines govern arrest and custody, Nilabati Behera relates to custodial death compensation, and M.C. Mehta relates to environmental law.
questions.explanation_hindi: सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने 'विशाखा बनाम राजस्थान राज्य' (1997) के ऐतिहासिक वाद में कार्यस्थल पर कामकाजी महिलाओं के यौन उत्पीड़न की रोकथाम के लिए पहली बार व्यापक एवं बाध्यकारी दिशानिर्देश जारी किए, जिन्हें 'विशाखा दिशा-निर्देश' (Vishaka Guidelines) कहा जाता है। न्यायालय ने संविधान के अनुच्छेद 14, 15, 19(1)(g) और 21 तथा अंतरराष्ट्रीय अभिसमय 'सिडौ' (CEDAW) के प्रावधानों का सहारा लेकर विधिक शून्यता को भरा। जब तक संसद द्वारा 2013 में पॉश अधिनियम पारित नहीं किया गया, तब तक संविधान के अनुच्छेद 141 के तहत विशाखा दिशा-निर्देश ही देश के कानून के रूप में लागू रहे। अन्य विकल्पों में डी.के. बासु दिशा-निर्देश गिरफ्तारी प्रक्रिया से, नीलाबाती बेहरा हिरासत में मृत्यु व मुआवजे से तथा एम.सी. मेहता पर्यावरण संरक्षण से संबंधित हैं।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (C) Vishaka Guidelines

questions.explanation_english: The Tax Deducted at Source (TDS) mechanism under Chapter XVII-B of the Income Tax Act, 1961 is anchored in the principle of 'Pay As You Earn' (PAYE). questions.question_english: Beyond the physical built environment, the RPwD Act, 2016 requires accessibility in information and communication technology (ICT). For school administration, what does this statutory mandate primarily imply?
options_english: Ensuring school websites and digital learning materials are fully accessible to CWSN
Providing mandatory separate high-speed internet connections exclusively for students with disabilities
Mandating that only specialized schools are required to invest in ICT accessibility infrastructure
Restricting digital accessibility mandates strictly to higher education and university institutions
questions.explanation_english: Section 42 of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 mandates that the appropriate Government ensure all content available in audio, print, and electronic media is accessible, and that electronic media is accessible through suitable formats. Read in conjunction with Section 16 (inclusive education), school administrations are legally obligated to ensure that institutional websites, ERP portals, admission forms, online examination systems, and digital learning materials (e-textbooks, learning management systems, multimedia modules) conform to accessibility standards (such as Web Content Accessibility Guidelines - WCAG 2.1 and GIGW). This ensures that Children with Special Needs (CWSN), including visually impaired and hearing impaired students, can navigate school resources seamlessly using screen readers and assistive tech.
questions.explanation_hindi: दिव्यांगजन अधिकार अधिनियम, 2016 की धारा 42 यह प्रावधान करती है कि सरकार यह सुनिश्चित करेगी कि ऑडियो, प्रिंट और इलेक्ट्रॉनिक मीडिया में उपलब्ध सभी सामग्रियां सुलभ प्रारूपों (accessible formats) में हों तथा दिव्यांगजनों की इलेक्ट्रॉनिक मीडिया तक आसान पहुंच हो। धारा 16 (समावेशी शिक्षा) के साथ पढ़ने पर, विद्यालय प्रशासन के लिए यह कानूनी दायित्व बनता है कि वह विद्यालय की वेबसाइटों, छात्र पोर्टलों, ऑनलाइन परीक्षा प्रणालियों और डिजिटल पाठ्य-सामग्रियों (ई-पुस्तकों, वीडियो पाठों) को भारतीय सरकारी वेबसाइट दिशानिर्देशों (GIGW) और WCAG मानकों के अनुरूप स्क्रीन-रीडर व सहायक तकनीकों के अनुकूल बनाए ताकि विशेष आवश्यकता वाले बच्चे (CWSN) उनका सुगमता से उपयोग कर सकें।

questions.question_english: The Supreme Court of India has consistently applied the principle of harmonious construction between Directive Principles and Fundamental Rights, reading Article 46 alongside which constitutional provision to sustain affirmative action and special educational measures for SCs and STs?
options_english: Article 15(4)
Article 19(1)(a)

questions.explanation_english:
The doctrine of harmonious construction is a foundational principle of Indian constitutional jurisprudence, establishing that Fundamental Rights (Part III) and Directive Principles (Part IV) must be construed together to achieve the constitutional goal of a welfare state.

Following the landmark ruling in State of Madras v. Champakam Dorairajan (1951), the First Constitutional Amendment Act, 1951 added clause (4) to Article 15. Article 15(4) enables the State to make 'any special provision for the advancement of any socially and educationally backward classes of citizens or for the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes.'

The Supreme Court has repeatedly held that Article 15(4) is an enabling provision designed to give effect to the directive principle enshrined in Article 46 (which obligates the State to promote with special care the educational and economic interests of SCs, STs, and weaker sections). By reading Article 46 alongside Article 15(4), the judiciary has upheld reservations in educational institutions, fee concessions, relaxation of qualifying marks, and special scholarship schemes against challenges alleging violations of formal equality under Article 15(1) or Article 29(2).
questions.explanation_hindi:
भारतीय संवैधानिक न्यायशास्त्र में सामंजस्यपूर्ण व्याख्या (harmonious construction) का सिद्धांत यह स्थापित करता है कि मौलिक अधिकार (भाग III) और नीति निर्देशक तत्व (भाग IV) एक-दूसरे के विरोधी नहीं, बल्कि पूरक हैं।

मद्रास राज्य बनाम चंपकम दोराइराजन (1951) के मामले के बाद प्रथम संविधान संशोधन अधिनियम, 1951 द्वारा अनुच्छेद 15 में खंड (4) जोड़ा गया। अनुच्छेद 15(4) राज्य को 'सामाजिक और शैक्षिक दृष्टि से पिछड़े वर्गों की उन्नति के लिए या अनुसूचित जातियों और अनुसूचित जनजातियों के लिए कोई विशेष उपबंध' करने की शक्ति प्रदान करता है।

सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने बार-बार यह निर्धारित किया है कि अनुच्छेद 15(4) वस्तुतः अनुच्छेद 46 में उल्लिखित नीति निर्देशक सिद्धांत (कमजोर वर्गों विशेषकर एससी और एसटी के शैक्षणिक व आर्थिक हितों की अभिवृद्धि) को क्रियान्वित करने का एक संवैधानिक साधन है। अनुच्छेद 46 और 15(4) को एक साथ पढ़कर ही शैक्षणिक संस्थानों में आरक्षण, शुल्क में छूट और विशेष छात्रवृत्तियों को समानता के अधिकार (अनुच्छेद 14 और 15(1)) के अनुरूप वैध ठहराया गया है।

questions.question_english: Under the unified Samagra Shiksha framework, a dedicated component exists for the Inclusive Education of Children with Special Needs (CWSN). Financial and pedagogical support under this component covers children across which grade levels?
options_english: Class I to Class VIII only
Class IX to Class XII only
Pre-primary up to Class XII
Class VI to Class X only
questions.explanation_english: Samagra Shiksha is an overarching integrated program formulated by the Ministry of Education that subsumed the erstwhile Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA), Rashtriya Madhyamik Shiksha Abhiyan (RMSA), and Teacher Education (TE). While earlier schemes restricted disability support to specific tiers (e.g., SSA covered elementary education from Classes I to VIII, and RMSA covered secondary Classes IX to XII), Samagra Shiksha adopted a continuous, unified continuum approach spanning from Pre-primary (pre-school) through Senior Secondary level (Class XII). Under its Inclusive Education component, CWSN covered under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016 receive early identification, assistive aids, transport/escort allowances, reader allowances, and specialized learning materials seamlessly from early childhood education up to Class XII.

questions.question_english:
Consider the following statements regarding the establishment and functioning of a "Resource Room" in an inclusive mainstream school:
I. It is a specialized instructional space where CWSN receive targeted, one-on-one or small group remedial instruction and therapeutic interventions.
II. It is equipped with specialized Teaching-Learning Materials (TLMs), assistive technologies, and adaptive learning devices.
III. CWSN spend their entire school day inside the resource room, segregated from their non-disabled peers.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
options_english: I and II only
II and III only
I and III only
I, II and III
questions.explanation_english: Statements I and II are correct, while Statement III is incorrect. In inclusive school models under Samagra Shiksha and NCERT guidelines, a Resource Room is an enriched, specialized pedagogical room within a mainstream school equipped with adaptive teaching-learning materials (TLMs), tactile books, Braille kits, speech therapy software, sensory integration aids, and developmental toys (Statement II). Children with Special Needs (CWSN) visit the resource room for specific designated periods during the week to receive remedial instruction, functional skill training, and therapeutic support from a qualified special educator (Statement I). Crucially, a resource room is NOT meant for permanent segregation. Confining CWSN to a separate room for the entire school day violates the foundational tenets of inclusive education and Section 16 of the RPwD Act, 2016; students spend the overwhelming majority of their day in general classrooms with non-disabled peers.
questions.explanation_hindi: कथन I और II सही हैं, जबकि कथन III गलत है। एनसीईआरटी एवं समग्र शिक्षा के समावेशी शिक्षा मॉडल के अनुसार, एक मुख्यधारा के स्कूल में 'रिसोर्स रूम' (संसाधन कक्ष) एक विशेष रूप से सुसज्जित कक्ष होता है, जिसमें ब्रेल उपकरण, स्पर्शनीय शिक्षण सामग्री (TLM), संवेदी उपकरण, सहायक तकनीकी और विकासात्मक खेल सामग्री उपलब्ध होती है (कथन II)। विशेष आवश्यकता वाले बच्चे (CWSN) सप्ताह में कुछ निर्धारित घंटों या कालखंडों (Periods) के लिए विशेष शिक्षक से उपचारात्मक शिक्षण, उपचारात्मक कौशल और व्यक्तिगत हस्तक्षेप प्राप्त करने हेतु रिसोर्स रूम आते हैं (कथन I)। तथापि, कथन III पूर्णतः गलत है क्योंकि रिसोर्स रूम का उद्देश्य बच्चों का पृथक्करण (Segregation) करना नहीं है। बच्चों को पूरे दिन रिसोर्स रूम में बंद रखना समावेशी शिक्षा के मूल सिद्धांतों तथा RPwD अधिनियम, 2016 की धारा 16 का उल्लंघन है; छात्र अपने विद्यालय समय का अधिकांश भाग सामान्य कक्षा में अपने गैर-दिव्यांग साथियों के साथ ही बिताते हैं।

questions.question_english:
Given below are two statements, one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): Most government scholarship schemes for socio-economically disadvantaged groups prescribe a minimum attendance benchmark (usually 75%) as a mandatory condition for annual renewal.
Reason (R): The primary policy intent behind welfare scholarships is to incentivize consistent classroom attendance and arrest dropout rates among marginalized student populations.
In the context of the statements above, which one of the following is correct?
options_english: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation_english: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct, and Reason (R) directly explains Assertion (A). Welfare scholarship schemes (such as Pre-Matric and Post-Matric Scholarships for SC, ST, OBC, and minority students) are designed not merely as unconditional cash transfers, but as targeted educational retention instruments. To ensure that students remain actively integrated into formal education and achieve learning milestones, guidelines mandate that the beneficiary must maintain at least 75% attendance during the academic session. questions.explanation_english:
Under Section 4(2)(c) of the POSH Act, 2013, the Internal Complaints Committee must include one external member nominated from amongst non-governmental organizations or associations committed to the cause of women, or a person familiar with issues relating to sexual harassment.

The purpose of this external member is precisely to prevent institutional cover-ups, management pressure, or bias by internal school administration.

questions.explanation_english: Under Entry 66(a) of Notification No. 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate) dated 28th June 2017, services provided by an educational institution to its students, faculty, and staff are completely exempt from GST. questions.question_english: What is the legal enforceability and constitutional status of the state directive provided under Article 46 of the Constitution of India?
options_english: It is directly enforceable through a writ of mandamus in the High Court under Article 226
It is non-justiciable in courts of law but fundamental in the governance of the country
It can only be enforced upon recommendation by the National Commission for Scheduled Castes
It is legally binding on private educational institutions but directory for government entities
questions.explanation_english:
Article 46 is part of the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) contained in Part IV of the Constitution of India. It enjoins the State to 'promote with special care the educational and economic interests of the weaker sections of the people, and, in particular, of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes, and shall protect them from social injustice and all forms of exploitation.'

Under Article 37, the provisions contained in Part IV are explicitly declared to be non-justiciable—that is, they 'shall not be enforceable by any court.' Consequently, no citizen can approach the Supreme Court (under Article 32) or a High Court (under Article 226) seeking a writ of mandamus to compel the State to legislate or enact a specific scheme under Article 46.

However, Article 37 emphatically adds that these principles are nonetheless 'fundamental in the governance of the country and it shall be the duty of the State to apply these principles in making laws.' Therefore, while non-justiciable in the judicial forum, Article 46 serves as an enduring constitutional guide and mandate for executive policy-making, legislative enactments, and affirmative administrative measures.
questions.explanation_hindi:
भारतीय संविधान के भाग IV में सन्निहित राज्य के नीति निर्देशक सिद्धांतों (DPSP) के अंतर्गत अनुच्छेद 46 यह निर्देश देता है कि 'राज्य जनता के दुर्बल वर्गों के, विशेषतया अनुसूचित जातियों और अनुसूचित जनजातियों के शिक्षा और अर्थ संबंधी हितों की विशेष सावधानी से अभिवृद्धि करेगा और सामाजिक अन्याय तथा सभी प्रकार के शोषण से उनका संरक्षण करेगा।'

संविधान के अनुच्छेद 37 के अनुसार, भाग IV के उपबंध किसी भी न्यायालय द्वारा प्रवर्तनीय (justiciable) नहीं होंगे। इसका अर्थ यह है कि नागरिक अनुच्छेद 46 के कार्यान्वयन हेतु सर्वोच्च न्यायालय (अनुच्छेद 32) या उच्च न्यायालय (अनुच्छेद 226) से परमादेश (writ of mandamus) जारी नहीं करवा सकते।

तथापि, अनुच्छेद 37 यह स्पष्ट रूप से घोषित करता है कि ये सिद्धांत 'देश के शासन में मूलभूत हैं और विधि बनाने में इन सिद्धांतों को लागू करना राज्य का कर्तव्य होगा।' इस प्रकार, यद्यपि यह न्यायालयों में गैर-वादयोग्य (non-justiciable) है, किंतु यह विधायिका और कार्यपालिका के लिए नीति-निर्माण और कल्याणकारी योजनाओं हेतु आधारभूत संवैधानिक अधिदेश है।

questions.question_english:
Consider the following statements regarding the recording of a child victim's statement under the POCSO Act, 2012:
I. The statement of the child should be recorded through audio-video electronic means, if possible.
II. The police officer must ensure that the child is comfortable and not exposed to trauma or fear during questioning.
III. The statement must strictly be recorded in English only for official court records.
IV. The statement can be recorded at the child's residence or a place of the child's choice.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
options_english: I, II, and IV only
I, II, and III only
II, III, and IV only
I, II, III, and IV
questions.explanation_english:
Under Section 24 and Section 26 of the POCSO Act, 2012, specific child-friendly procedures are mandated for recording the child victim's statement:
- Statement I is correct: Section 24(4) provides that the police officer shall record the statement of the child by audio-video electronic means, whenever possible.
- Statement II is correct: Section 24(3) stipulates that the investigating police officer must ensure that the child is not exposed in any way to the accused, is not subjected to fear or trauma, and that questioning is conducted in a reassuring, comfortable atmosphere. Section 24(2) also mandates that the officer must not be in police uniform.
- Statement III is incorrect: There is no requirement whatsoever that the statement must be in English. Section 24(5) and Section 26 clearly establish that the statement must be recorded in the language understood and spoken by the child. Where necessary, the assistance of a certified translator, interpreter, special educator, or child psychologist must be arranged.
- Statement IV is correct: Section 24(1) expressly provides that the statement shall be recorded at the child's residence or at a place of the child's choice, preferably by a woman police officer not below the rank of sub-inspector.
Therefore, Statements I, II, and IV are correct, while Statement III is false.
questions.explanation_hindi:
सही उत्तर A (केवल I, II और IV) है।

पॉक्सो (POCSO) अधिनियम, 2012 की धारा 24 और 26 में बालक के बयान दर्ज करने हेतु बाल-अनुकूल (Child-friendly) वैधानिक प्रक्रिया निर्धारित की गई है:
- कथन I सही है: धारा 24(4) के अनुसार, यदि संभव हो तो बालक का बयान ऑडियो-वीडियो इलेक्ट्रॉनिक माध्यम से दर्ज किया जाना चाहिए।
- कथन II सही है: धारा 24(3) के अनुसार, पुलिस अधिकारी यह सुनिश्चित करेगा कि पूछताछ के दौरान बच्चे को किसी प्रकार का भय या मानसिक आघात (Trauma) न पहुंचे। धारा 24(2) के तहत पुलिस अधिकारी वर्दी में नहीं होगा।
- कथन III गलत है: पॉक्सो अधिनियम में ऐसी कोई बाध्यता नहीं है कि बयान केवल अंग्रेजी में दर्ज हो। धारा 24(5) और धारा 26 के तहत बयान उस भाषा में दर्ज किया जाता है जिसे बच्चा समझता और बोलता है। आवश्यकता पड़ने पर दुभाषिए (Interpreter), अनुवादक या विशेष शिक्षक की सहायता ली जाती है।
- कथन IV सही है: धारा 24(1) के अनुसार, बयान बच्चे के निवास स्थान पर या उसकी पसंद के किसी अन्य स्थान पर, जहां तक संभव हो महिला पुलिस अधिकारी (जो उप-निरीक्षक से निम्न पद की न हो) द्वारा दर्ज किया जाएगा।
अतः कथन I, II और IV सही हैं।
